extraction_scope: Worker-6 adjudicated mechanism ontology from source text, primary Tables 1-3, local supplement, figure captions, and database rows. Mechanism strength is bounded because membrane permeation and efflux inhibition are supported by phenotypic potentiation plus in silico modelling, not direct transport or membrane-damage assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Most peptides had minimal intrinsic antimicrobial activity, while selected short cationic peptides potentiated novobiocin against susceptible and multidrug-resistant E. coli.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports potentiation/low intrinsic MIC profile, not a direct membrane or efflux mechanism by itself.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The authors propose enhanced novobiocin uptake through peptide-novobiocin complex formation and amphipathic surface character.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism remains model-supported; no direct membrane permeability or uptake assay value was found in local materials.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Docking to AcrB/RND efflux pump supports a possible efflux-inhibition component for compounds 6 and 27 through loop-region interactions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No direct efflux-pump transport/inhibition assay was present locally; classify as computational support, not direct mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Norfloxacin combination results did not show comparable potentiation, which the authors use as a negative-control pattern for the novobiocin-specific hypothesis.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Supports specificity of the potentiation pattern; does not directly prove the proposed mechanism.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Mechanistic claims are bounded to in silico docking/MD plus MIC potentiation; no local direct membrane-permeability, LPS-binding, or efflux inhibition assay was found.
